newsitem.title: USA: Calif. budget talks drag on, some progress made.
newsitem.headline: Calif. budget talks drag on, some progress made.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson and legislative leaders made progress Friday in budget negotiations, but said a final agreement ending the impasse could be a week or more away.
Wilson, a Republican, and Senate President Bill Lockyer, a Democrat, said Friday's "Big Five" meeting was productive. The Big Five includes the governor and senior legislative leaders.

"We continue to meet with the legislative leaders to reach a final budget for California," Wilson spokesman Ron Low said. "They're making progress on the issue of welfare, and they're expected to meet again on Sunday."
Lockyer said a final agreement was at least a week away.

Welfare reform has been the major stumbling block for lawmakers negotiating the state's budget for the 1997-1998 fiscal year, which began July 1. The state's Constitutional budget deadline was June 15.
